units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Oh. Oh, that's quiet.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. You've stepped through a small passage and left the city behind.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This is the Begijnhof. A hidden courtyard of small houses around a green lawn.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: It feels like a different century.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In a way, yes. Please talk softly, if you talk at all.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: These are people's homes.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Right. Whispering then.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Whispering is fine. Now, who lived here?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Beguines. Lay Catholic women who lived together, devoted to prayer and charity, but who were not nuns.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: When did it start?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's unclear exactly. A beguine house is mentioned in a document from 1346, and a courtyard in 1389.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So we say, by the late 14th century at the latest.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. And the miracle?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the story behind the Stille Omgang.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Here's the tradition. In March 1345, a gravely ill man was given the last rites.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He vomited up the communion host.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The priest wrapped it and put it in the fire.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The next morning, the host was found unburnt in the ashes.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That sounds like a legend.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. It's tradition. The earliest sources of the story are a matter for historians, and the details we gave are the version people tell.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Even the retellings say "allegedly."

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So, record, or legend?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Legend, in its details. What is documented is that the devotion to it grew, that pilgrims came, and that it shaped the city's religious life.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A procession, the Silent Procession, still commemorates it every March.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Legend. Point to me?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Point to you.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the houses?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Look for number 34. It's called Het Houten Huys, the Wooden House.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It dates from about 1420, and it's the oldest wooden house in Amsterdam.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One of only two wooden houses still standing in the center.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Because of fires.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. Wooden houses were banned after big fires.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This one survived.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And there's a church.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Two. In 1578, when the city turned Protestant, the beguines' chapel was closed for about 30 years, then given to English Presbyterians.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's known as the English Church.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the other?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Across from it, a hidden Catholic church.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1671 the architect Philip Vingboons converted two houses into a church that could not be recognized from the outside.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Catholics could worship, quietly.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Today it's called the Miracle Church, from 1908.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A secret church. That's the record?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the record.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, so now the ghost story. You promised.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. This one is a legend. It's about a woman named Cornelia Arens.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: She was a beguine, and she died on 14 October 1654.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That date is certain?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's the date given for her death.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The legend is about her burial.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The story says she wanted to be buried in the church.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The church was Protestant by then.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So she was buried in the gutter outside.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: In the gutter. Outside the door.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the legend, and the details vary in the retelling.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Today a red stone slab lies in the gutter outside the chapel, often with flowers on it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Ah. So is she the ghost?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We don't say that. We say it's a legend about a burial.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We can't prove the coffin story.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We can't prove the stone marks her grave.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We just tell you what's told.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Legend, legend.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Legend. Stamped.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the last beguine?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Not her. The last beguine was Sister Antonia, whose name was Agatha Kaptein.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: She died on 23 May 1971.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's recent.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. And that's the record.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The residents today?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Women, but no longer nuns. It's a quiet place, so we'll leave it quiet.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Tally. Ghosts, one, if you count the legend.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: I count it as a legend. Real history, four.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Legends, two.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I'm changing the tally. Record versus legend.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Not ghosts.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Better.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Last stop. Where?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Back out through the passage. Go north-west, along the Singel canal, then across to the Keizersgracht.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Number 123. It's a tall, elegant house on the canal, with six stone heads along its front.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Six heads. Of course.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And one of the oldest murder legends in town.
